fact: The health ministry's E-Health Strategy 2012-2017 names the District Health Information System (DHIS) as the national HMIS and lists its strengthening among the e-health applications under way; the document is undated, so the year is its published date.

The health ministry's E-Health Strategy 2012-2017 states that the DHIS is deployed throughout the country and captures data from all 67 districts, with mobile phones being added for remote facilities reporting to the national database; it does not say in so many words where the data is keyed, and the year is the undated document's published date.

The health ministry's E-Health Strategy 2012-2017 says mobile phones are being used in remote facilities to report to the national DHIS database but gives no number or share of facilities doing so; the year is the undated document's published date.

The Countdown to 2030 synthesis report, written with Ministry of Health and Child Care staff, calls the routine system 'the MoHCC HMIS' and says a study was run on the private sector's readiness to report through it; no date is given for this, so the document's published date is used.

The report states that the national reporting rate of health facility data in DHIS2 was above 92% in 2024, with only Harare and Bulawayo provinces just below the 90% threshold, and that the number of districts meeting that threshold rose over 2019-2024; no numerator or denominator is given and it does not say who keys the reports.

A DHIS2 Community of Practice abstract (primary author Shepherd Maverudze) states that the Impilo EHR is deployed across over 700 facilities; it gives no denominator and no breakdown by tier, and no date, so the document's published date is used.

The abstract states that Impilo captures real-time clinical and administrative data for services including HIV testing, antiretroviral therapy and maternal and child health, and that facility data is stored in centralised repositories and a national data warehouse; it does not say a record can be retrieved at another facility. No date is given, so the document's published date is used.

The abstract states that data from Impilo facilities flows to DHIS2 by three pipelines (real-time for connected facilities, mobile backups for offline synchronisation, manual backups elsewhere), with middleware updating DHIS2 aggregate data and tracker programmes and reporting on over 150 indicators and 15 facility registers; this covers Impilo facilities only, and how other facilities report is not stated. The document's published date is used.

The Permanent Secretary for Health and Child Care, Dr Aspect Maunganidze, told The Sunday Mail that the Impilo EHR had been deployed at 1,178 health facilities since 2021, at varied levels of adoption and uptake: Bulawayo 23, Harare 53, Manicaland 225, Mashonaland Central 88, Mashonaland East 111, Mashonaland West 148, Masvingo 158, Matabeleland North 79, Matabeleland South 135 and Midlands 158; no denominator is given and the count covers hospitals as well as clinics.

The Permanent Secretary says the 1,178 facilities with Impilo are spread across provinces and districts and include clinics, hospitals and other health centres; the level of the hospitals is not stated and no count is given by type.

The Sunday Mail describes Impilo as the national electronic health record system, developed by a local technical team, with the Ministry of Health and Child Care's Permanent Secretary speaking for its rollout and the ICT ministry, the higher education ministry and Potraz named as contributing government agencies.

The article says significant financial and technical support for Impilo has come from donor funding and implementing partners, alongside contributions from three government agencies; it names no donor, no amount and no domestic budget line.

The U.S. President's Malaria Initiative profile states that monthly HMIS data collection is paper-based at village, health facility and hospital levels, and that the paper records go to the district, where the district health information officer enters them into the Zimbabwe DHIS2; no date is given, so the document's published year is used.

PMI states that monthly HMIS collection at health facility level is on paper, keyed at the district; its routine table gives 1,776 health facilities reporting into the HMIS/DHIS2 in 2022 (1,758 in 2018) with 96% of expected monthly reports received (97.2% in 2018), which counts reports received and not facilities entering them.

PMI states that the HMIS collects routine aggregate health information from four levels of the health system: primary (over 1,700 health centres, clinics and rural hospitals), secondary (about 140 district-level hospitals), tertiary (eight provincial hospitals) and quaternary (six hospitals); all report on paper. The document's published year is used.

PMI describes DHIS2 as the Ministry of Health and Child Care's system: donors and partners have very limited access to it, the ministry circulates no routine monthly DHIS2 report, and the malaria programme shares its data with PMI at bilateral meetings. The document's published year is used.

PMI states that electronic health records designed for deployment at each health facility, from which patient-level data would be aggregated into DHIS2, had been piloted in a small number of select districts, with no count given, and that the country continued to rely mainly on the existing paper-based HMIS. The document's published year is used.

PMI gives full digitisation of the HMIS through facility electronic health records as the current strategic direction of the Ministry of Health and Child Care, and says it is unclear whether the very substantial resources needed for scale-up will be made available. The document's published year is used.

The Ministry of Health and Child Care's National Health Strategy 2021-2025 commits to supporting the deployment of the electronic health record (Impilo) system, alongside health ICT infrastructure and broadband connectivity at all levels and a start on digitising the community health strategy; no costing is in the passages, and the strategy's published year is used.

The ministry's own strategy lists the Impilo Electronic Health Record among its routine patient-level reporting systems and takes its deployment as a ministry undertaking; the strategy's published year is used.

The National Health Strategy 2021-2025 names DHIS2 among the ministry's routine aggregate systems for monitoring and evaluation and plans an Electronic Logistics Management Information System linked to the electronic health record and DHIS2, with private facilities' consumption linked separately; the strategy's published year is used.
The strategy cites 'MoHCC DHIS2 2019' as the source of its service figures and lists DHIS2 among the ministry's own routine aggregate systems; the strategy's published year is used.
